title: Ferdinand II to Garcilaso de la Vega, ambassador in Rome: the ten-line postscript in a second cipher
correspondents: Ferdinand II of Aragon → Garcilaso de la Vega, ambassador in Rome (letter also inserts one to the ambassador in Naples, Joan Escrivà)
shelfmark: Barcelona, ACA, Diversos, Sástago 193 (Lío B), nº 79/83 (DECODE R10180, 7 pp.)
folio_note: Only the last ten lines are unread; the rest of the letter is printed deciphered in Parisi 2004 (Pedralbes 24, p. 115 of the PDF per Tomokiyo).
status: Cryptoole IT1498-1 (open). Cryptiana unsolved.htm: the letter was deciphered by Parisi (2004), 'but the last ten lines are in a different cipher and is left undeciphered'; Galende Díaz (1994) mentions a cipher of Garcilaso de la Vega preserved in the archives. DECODE R10180 (Mikael Hammarlind's note): Parisi doc. 83, two hands and two cryptographic systems, the inserted Escrivà/Naples section in Parisi's published corpus. DECODE marks it Non-decrypted. Attempted here 26 Oct 2026 (targets/garcilaso1498): both passages transcribed; all BRAH 9/15 keys (on DECODE as R9815-R9832), the Escrivà ciphers and the Cifra general excluded; ciphertext-only fails at 315 signs. Key likely in RAH Salazar A-11 ff. 109-111 / 121-125 (Garcilaso's deciphered 1496 letters).
why: Ferdinand's instructions to his Rome ambassador in summer 1498, under Alexander VI and on the eve of the French invasion of Italy.

title: William, Baron Craven, to Prince Rupert, The Hague
correspondents: William Craven, 1st Baron Craven → Prince Rupert
shelfmark: BL Add MS 18982 ff. 134–135 (DECODE R8447, 3 pp.)
status: Cryptoole XX1648-1 (open). Cryptiana unsolved.htm: 'While most of the undeciphered ciphertexts in this volume can be read by using deciphered letters or with known keys, this seems to use some different cipher.' DECODE R8447: English clear text, numerical symbols, Non-decrypted, images by login. targets/rupert screened the Add MS 72438 keys against the 1645–46 letters only; R8447 was not transcribed.
why: Craven was the exiled royal family's chief financial backer and Elizabeth of Bohemia's confidant; the letter dates from the months Rupert took command of the revolted royalist fleet.

title: Barrière–Condé intercepts: 15 September 1654 and 18 June 1655
correspondents: Barrière → Louis II de Bourbon, Prince of Condé (15 Sept 1654); Condé → Barrière (18 Jun 1655)
shelfmark: BL Add MS 4200 f. 98 (DECODE R8395, 1 p.); short ciphertext f. 101 (DECODE R8398, 1 p.)
folio_note: Add MS 4200 holds eleven Condé–Barrière letters of 1654–55; the 1655 ones use the f. 108 cipher (R8405+R8406), incl. undated f. 96 (R8394).
status: Cryptoole XX1654-1 (open). Cryptiana unsolved.htm and louisxiv0.htm ('Prince of Condé (1654-1655)'): the 1654 letter f. 98 seems undeciphered and in a different cipher from the known 1655 Condé–Barrière cipher (f. 108); whether f. 101 reads with the 1655 key is untested. DECODE R8395/R8398: Thurloe papers volume, clear text in English and French, images by login. Copies of Condé–Barrière letters (partly cipher) are also in Bodleian MS. Rawl. A (Thurloe papers). Reviewed 20 Oct 2026: R8395 is Barrière to Condé, as the manuscript heading/source list state; R8398 is the reverse direction. Both images and R8405/R8406 key images retrieved. No validated diacritic-preserving reading established.
why: Condé, in Spanish service after the Fronde, courting Cromwell through his London agent in the year of the Anglo-French rapprochement; Thurloe intercepted the letter.
language: French (some clear text translated into English)

title: Sir Edward Hyde to 'Mr Milles', intercepted letter with code numbers and a cover-name list
correspondents: Sir Edward Hyde → 'Mr Milles' (cover name)
shelfmark: BL Add MS 4166, ff. 92-93 (DECODE R4886); printed Thurloe State Papers vii 775-776
folio_note: f. 92 clear except cover names ('Mr Mills' = Hyde, 'Edmundson' = Charles Stuart); f. 93 code numbers, then a list of number groups each followed by a cover name
status: Cryptoole XX1659-1 (open). DECODE R4886 'Non-decrypted', a copy, access login; BL images 'currently unavailable'. About 133 numerals, 103 distinct, max 966 (Turner's census of the print). The same volume holds key records R4887-R4913 (f. 95 code list naming Ignatius White and the Duke of Gloucester; numerical ciphers ff. 96-117).
why: An intercepted royalist letter from Hyde six months before the Restoration, with what looks like a cover-name table that would give cribs.

title: Other cipher sheets in the Ferdinand III family-correspondence record (DECODE R1579, images I7060, I7066, I7068)
correspondents: Emperor Ferdinand III → Archduke Leopold Wilhelm (the record's dated letter); senders of the other sheets unknown
shelfmark: Vienna, HHStA, Familienkorrespondenz A, Karton 11 (DECODE R1579)
folio_note: I7060: two-/three-digit and two-/three-letter codes; I7066: blocks in a simple-looking symbol cipher; I7068: longer text in a similar cipher (negative image)
status: Cryptoole AT1640-1 (open). DECODE R1579 'Non-decrypted', 4 pages, access login. Tomokiyo says these sheets are in a different cipher from the Ferdinand III-Leopold Wilhelm cipher read by Ernst (2018).

title: English royalist letter in numerical code, September 1645 (SP 106/10 f. 251)
correspondents: Unknown sender → unknown recipient
shelfmark: TNA, State Papers, inv.nr. 106 box 10, f. 251 · DECODE R931
status: Attempted, open (21 Sept 2026; own entry sp106r931 since 14 Oct 2026). Of the four DECODE records first grouped here, R722 is the 1625 Venetian letter of the SP 106/10 codebreaker's file (now sp106r722, catalogue 66) and R656 and R662 are that codebreaker's worksheet and memorandum on it. Left here: R931, a strip of ~190 numbers 10-260 with clear words ('(1) septembre 1645', 'earnestly', 'reasons'), 104 distinct numbers: a nomenclator. Lasry's 1645-46 SP 106 keys, the R932 Goring key and the Charles I-Culpeper 1645 key (R9117/R9118) do not fit.
why: A royalist despatch of autumn 1645, after Naseby; what it says is not known.

title: Letters to Mr Carré, Pall Mall, 1742–45, 3 ciphertexts
correspondents: Anonymous sender → Mr Carré, Pall Mall, London
status: Viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/carre1742/, split on 14 Oct 2026 from bl32305, where it had been folded into item 78). R2968/R2970/R2972 (letters to Mr Carré, Pall Mall, Mar 1742, received 22 Aug 1742, 19 Jan 1745): transcribed in full (1323 groups, 381 distinct, 1–800); not a letter cipher (anneal = shuffled control), not one-part (r = −0.26): two-part code of ~800 entries, closed; R2969 is a frequency count, not a key.
why: Three anonymous letters to a Mr Carré in Pall Mall, intercepted 1742–45, entirely in a code with no gloss; what they hide is not known.

title: Giuliano Caprile (Eger) to Bonaventura Pistofilo, 9 March 1519
correspondents: Giuliano Caprile → Bonaventura Pistofilo / Alfonso I 'Este
shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori b. 4/23, 1, Envoy reports, Ferrara
status: DECODE R1128: seven lines in Caprile's 1519 two-tier cipher (a small letter over a base sign), no decipherment. Worked 21 Sept and 2 Oct 2026 (targets/caprile1519/, attempted, open: the 1519 tables rebuilt from R1133/7c and R1130/4c give no signal on R1128). The rest of the item is resolved: R1129–R1135 have 1882 decipherments (b/c on Vestigia); the 1520–21 letters (R1136, R1138, R1139) are another cipher, read in part in targets/caprile1520/ (split 14 Oct 2026). Subject, from the clear part and the next letter: Caprile's own lawsuit at Rome. Key obtainable from the 1882 decipherments of nos. 3–8 and 10.
why: A Ferrarese agent at Eger, the Hungarian see held by Ippolito d'Este, writing to Ferrara in 1519–21 on Hungarian affairs on the eve of Mohács.

title: Elia da Cortona (1180-1253) (Venice?) to unknown recipient
correspondents: Elia da Cortona (1180-1253) → unknown recipient
shelfmark: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Mellon MS 29
status: DECODE R2877: Non-decrypted. Attempted here 22 Sept 2026 (targets/mellon29/): not a letter but the pseudo-Elian alchemical codex Lumen luminum, c. 1525; cipher only on ff. 1v-2v (zodiac 'se chiama' table and two recipe lists, ~234 letters) plus a later pastedown copy; Latin letters, not graphic signs. Simple substitution (with a working control), homophonic, progressive, Vigenère and Alberti-disk attacks fail; possibly invented secret names. Needs a clear copy of the prologue's recipes.

title: Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von to unknown recipient
correspondents: Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von → unknown recipient
shelfmark: National Library of Sweden
status: DECODE R4350: Non-decrypted. Viewed 22 Sept 2026: the record is the whole Murberg volume (KB I.g.18, 114 images); the cipher is five passages (809 numeric groups 1-848, 175 distinct) inside a German peace memorandum of 1717 on Poland, the Czar and Norway (PDF pp. 34-41). No decipherment on the pages; the only Görtz key on DECODE (R7691, BL Add MS 32287 f.2, 1716) is a French 4-digit code, not this one. Ciphertext-only annealing (homophonic letter, alphabetical syllabary) failed, and failed its synthetic control. Needs Görtz's German chancery key (Riksarkivet Görtz papers). See targets/goertz1717/.
why: Ciphered letter of Murberg, Johan, Görtz, Georg Heinrich von to unknown recipient, 1717; what the cipher hides is not known.
